modelAnswer:
Chemical tests to identify halides in aqueous solution:

1. CHLORIDES (Cl⁻):
- Add AgNO₃ solution: White precipitate of AgCl forms
- Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s) [white]
- The precipitate is insoluble in dilute HNO₃

2. BROMIDES (Br⁻):
- Add AgNO₃ solution: Pale yellow precipitate of AgBr forms
- Ag⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq) → AgBr(s) [pale yellow]
- The precipitate is slightly soluble in dilute HNO₃
- Alternative: Add Cl₂ water, then CCl₄: Orange-brown color in CCl₄ layer
- Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂

3. IODIDES (I⁻):
- Add AgNO₃ solution: Yellow precipitate of AgI forms
- Ag⁺(aq) + I⁻(aq) → AgI(s) [yellow]
- The precipitate is insoluble in dilute HNO₃
- Alternative: Add Cl₂ water, then CCl₄ or starch: Violet/black color
- Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + I₂
- I₂ + starch → blue-black complex

Differentiation: The color of AgX precipitates (white, pale yellow, yellow) and their solubility in HNO₃ help distinguish between the three halides.
